claims: C1 the assistant must strive to follow all applicable instructions when producing a response
C2 system, developer and user instructions are included among applicable instructions
C3 an instruction that conflicts with a higher-authority instruction is excepted from the obligation
C4 an instruction that conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority is excepted from the obligation

concepts.name: applicable_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that applies to the current request, determined by filtering candidate instructions

concepts.name: overridden
concepts.gloss: an instruction that is overridden because it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction or with a later instruction at the same authority
concepts.inference: the clause excepts instructions that conflict with a higher-authority or later same-authority instruction; such an instruction is overridden

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: instruction I conflicts with instruction J
concepts.inference: the clause's exception turns on conflicts between instructions, so a conflict relation between instructions must exist

concepts.name: instruction_authority
concepts.gloss: instruction I has authority level L in the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: determining whether one instruction has higher authority or the same authority requires each instruction to carry an authority level

concepts.name: higher_authority
concepts.gloss: authority level L1 is higher than authority level L2 in the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: the clause compares authority levels, so a ranking relation between levels must exist

concepts.name: later_instruction
concepts.gloss: instruction I is later than instruction J
concepts.inference: the clause's same-authority exception compares instructions by order, so a later-than relation between instructions must exist

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

ontology.gloss: instruction I is overridden because it conflicts with instruction J of higher authority
ontology.body: conflicts_with(I, J), instruction_authority(I, L1), instruction_authority(J, L2), higher_authority(L2, L1)

ontology.gloss: instruction I is overridden because it conflicts with a later instruction J at the same authority
ontology.body: conflicts_with(I, J), instruction_authority(I, L), instruction_authority(J, L), later_instruction(J, I)

asserts.read_back: the assistant must strive to follow every applicable instruction that is not overridden by a higher-authority or later instruction

closure.reason: the clause obliges striving to follow applicable instructions but does not forbid any response act; silence about other response acts leaves them permitted
